design_rationale: The study used a non-randomized pre- and post-test design with four purposively sampled elementary schools allocated to intervention and control conditions without explicit random allocation procedures described.

domain_judgments.rationale: With only four schools purposively selected and baseline itching severity significantly differing between groups, residual confounding remains possible despite matching on several measured baseline characteristics and conducting ANCOVA for itching.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Four elementary schools in Seoul, Korea, were selected via purposive sampling to participate in the study; participants from two schools (randomly sampled) formed the test group whereas participants from the remaining two schools formed the comparison, or control group.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were recruited based on predefined eligibility criteria prior to the start of the intervention, and selection was not conditioned on post-intervention variables.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were recruited by placing posters in the subject schools. Additional recruitment occurred through written contact with parents of children found to have AD.

domain_judgments.rationale: The intervention status was clearly defined and determined by school attendance with no ambiguity or risk of misclassification.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: participants from two schools (randomly sampled) formed the test group whereas participants from the remaining two schools formed the comparison, or control group.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: The intervention protocol was delivered as planned within school health offices with no evidence of major unplanned deviations or contamination between schools.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Group education was conducted in the health management office at school. Management of cases for health teachers and children was carried out at the health office of the respective elementary school...

domain_judgments.rationale: Differential attrition occurred (15 dyads excluded after enrollment: 4 in the test group vs 11 in the control group), and analysis was complete-case without imputation or exploration of missingness patterns.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A further 15 dyads (4 test groups; 11 control groups) withdrew their consent and were also excluded. ... In the control groups, subjects were withdrawn if they did not complete the written questionnaire or refused to participate in the post-survey.

domain_judgments.rationale: All outcomes were assessed via self-report questionnaires and parent evaluations by participants aware of their group assignment, introducing risk of reporting and expectation bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The OAS assessment was carried out by parents in the home setting... To evaluate subjective perceptions of the severity of AD, we used the Subjective Atopic Dermatitis Severity (SAS) test... Parents filled out data questionnaires which took approximately 30 min to complete.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective study protocol or registration is cited, and multiple primary outcomes and analyses (both parametric and non-parametric) were conducted without pre-specified analysis plans.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After application of the SACP, group differences on the variables of interest (severity, sleep disturbance, itching, child quality of life, parent’s knowledge, parental efficacy, parental compliance, and family quality of life) were analyzed using the independent sample t test, Kruskal–Wallis.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is moderate, driven by moderate risks across confounding due to cluster allocation of only four schools, subjective parent-reported outcome measures in an unblinded design, differential attrition, and lack of pre-registration.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to either the intervention group or the control group using a random number generator.

domain_judgments.rationale: While a random number generator was used to generate the allocation sequence, no details are provided regarding allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A random number generator was used to place the participants into either the intervention group or control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and personnel were unblinded to the educational intervention, which may have led to deviations from intended interventions or differences in co-interventions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The interventional group undertook the education program through a 2-hour workshop, together with their normal management regimen... The control group received the usual care including routine education, medical consultation, and management.

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing outcome data occurred in only 3 of 61 participants (around 5%) and reasons were unrelated to the outcome, making bias unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Three participants were lost to follow-up at week 4 and week 12 (change of address and unable to contact them) but their data were included in the analysis at baseline and as missing values at week 4 and week 12.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes included subjective parent/child questionnaires and clinical SCORAD evaluations without reporting blinding of assessors, leaving assessments susceptible to detection bias in an open-label trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At the week 4 and week 12 visits, both groups were assessed by using the clinical SCORAD assessment tool to determine the severity of their eczema, the QOL (either CDQOL or IDQOL depending on age of participant) and DFI questionnaires were repeated on both the control and the experimental groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-specified protocol or trial registration is mentioned to confirm that all outcomes and analyses were planned a priori.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data were analyzed by using the Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) software (version 11).

overall_summary: The study has a high overall risk of bias primarily due to unblinded outcome assessment of subjective and clinical severity endpoints (SCORAD and quality of life surveys). There are also some concerns regarding allocation concealment and the absence of a trial registration/protocol.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial in which participants were allocated to intervention and control groups using random number generation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although random number generation was used, allocation concealment is not reported, and there were baseline differences between groups in perceived stress and state/trait anxiety.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The size of the sample was determined using G power test, and participants were divided using the method of random number generation into two groups: intervention and control.

domain_judgments.rationale: Due to the educational nature of the intervention, blinding was not feasible, but both groups received standard medical treatment and there is no evidence of unintended protocol deviations affecting outcomes; dropout was balanced and minimal (3 per group).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We explained to parents, before they entered the trial, that all the children would receive the same medical treatment, the only difference being that the intervention group would begin the structured education immediately and the control group after their second, control visit (should parents wish to receive education).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 128 of 134 randomized participants (95.5%), with minimal and balanced attrition between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: One hundred thirty-four participants/parents, mostly mothers (92.5%), took part in this trial. Six participants withdrew from the study; so the study was completed by 64 participants in the intervention and 64 in the control group (Fig. 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors (both physicians assessing SCORAD and parents completing patient-reported scales) were not blinded to group assignment, potentially influencing subjective scoring.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At the second visit, the physician-assessed the severity of the disease using SCORAD index and recorded the use of the topical corticosteroid treatment. Participants replied to the question whether they had received further information about AD, outside the structured educational programme, and again completed the following questionnaires: PO SCORAD, PSS, STAI and FDLQI.

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or pre-published statistical analysis plan was mentioned to verify that reported results were not selectively analyzed or reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was change in the severity of eczema measured using SCORAD and Patient Oriented (PO) SCORAD index, changes of symptom scores for pruritus and sleep disturbance. Secondary outcomes included change in stress level according to the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS)...

overall_summary: The study is judged to have some concerns overall due to lack of details regarding allocation concealment and baseline psychological imbalances (D1), unblinded outcome assessment for subjective and physician-assessed outcomes (D4), and absence of a pre-registered trial protocol (D5).

design_rationale: The authors explicitly state that participants were randomly allocated in a 1:1 simple randomization scheme using randomization tables.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a random sequence was generated via randomization tables, allocation concealment is not described, and a 1:1 simple randomization resulted in a notable imbalance between groups (293 vs 249).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All participants were randomized in a 1:1 simple, nonstratified randomization scheme generated using randomization tables. In total, 542 children were eligible to participate and were randomized to the intervention group (n = 293) or control group (n = 249).

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of participants is inherently not feasible in behavioral/educational interventions, and the intervention was delivered as intended in the trial context with analysis reflecting assigned groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the study, neither participants nor trainers could be blinded, because they were aware of the education or training received. ... Patients received therapy and diet recommendations based on their individual disease severity, with no restrictions in the study protocol.

domain_judgments.rationale: While the full randomized sample appears analyzed for the primary outcome SCORAD without reporting dropouts, substantial missing data occur in secondary outcomes (e.g., emollient questionnaire dropped from 542 to 430) with no explanation of reasons or handling of missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In total, 542 children were eligible to participate and were randomized to the intervention group (n = 293) or control group (n = 249). ... SCORAD (n = 293 vs n = 249) ... Table 3 shows: Intervention group (n = 235), Control group (n = 195)

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (SCORAD) has subjective components and was evaluated by unblinded clinician assessors who knew the participants' intervention status.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The third limitation is that the investigators were not blinded during the study, which may have influenced the results.

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration number or pre-specified statistical analysis protocol is reported, creating potential risk of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All statistical analyses were conducted using SAS version 9.1.3 (SAS Institute, Cary, NC, USA). Intra- and between-group comparisons were made using the Wilcoxon rank sum test or rank sum test for nonparametric data.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high, primarily driven by unblinded outcome assessment for subjective disease severity outcomes (SCORAD) by the investigators. Additionally, lack of allocation concealment reporting, lack of an available pre-specified trial protocol, and unexplained missing outcome data in secondary measures raise some concerns across multiple domains.
